abstract: The paper is dealing with the electromagnetic behavior analysis of high-speed synchronous reluctance machines (HS-SynRM), designed for the turbo-charger application. The transition from a first topology to other three variants is made based on the windings, slots and rotor shape, while the produced torque, the ripples, the power density and the efficiency are evaluated. The analysis is employed by means of numerical computation, based on fmite element method (FEM). A best suited topology is identified and considered for future evaluation and construction.

articleTitle: Impact of the Electric Vehicle Sector’s Development on Romania’s National Power System
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In the quest for achieving climate neutrality the development of the electric vehicle (EV) sector plays a significant role. While in Europe EV adoption is well encouraged by various political decisions, the transition toward electric mobility encounters numerous challenges. Among these challenges, the impact of the development of this sector on the national power systems is yet to be evaluated. In this context, this paper aims to analyze the impact of the EV sector development in Romania, considering the prognosis for 2030, on the national power system, in terms of power load increase and the total amount of electricity required. The analysis was conducted considering several scenarios regarding the charging regimes of the EV batteries, and the number of charges per week. While there are obviously some uncertainties about how things will look in 2030, the results of this study can offer some valuable insights into the potential measures that must be considered to sustain the development of the EV sector.

articleTitle: Modernization Solutions for the Trolleybus Traction Stations in the Chisinau Municipality
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents the current status and modernization of DC traction stations for powering trolleybuses. Most of the traction stations are over 50 years old and have a rigid structure, obsolete rectification equipment, and require colossal maintenance costs. Flexible power circuit structures, efficient electrical and electronic equipment, automated digital control systems, reactive energy compensation and trolleybus braking energy recovery have been proposed to modernise traction stations. The proposed modernization solutions will allow to increase the operating functionality and energy efficiency by about 30%, compatibility with the supplier’s electricity grid, reduction of operating costs of trolleybus traction stations.

articleTitle: Design of an Electronic Direct Drive Automotive Differential using Axial Flux PSMS with Sensorless Direct Torque and Flux Control
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Today, power electronics and digital computing together with electric drives technology are enabling new solutions for more controllable and efficient transportation systems. In this paper, we propose a new solution for the replacement of the traditional (mechanical differential) with an electronic differential based on the use of dual motors with axial flux PMSM. The control method of the two axial flux PMSM rotors is based on a direct flux and torque method. The direct torque and flux control method applied to the axial flux PMSM machine is capable of providing the necessary dynamical performance during transient regimes.

articleTitle: High Gain Patch Antenna Array for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper, a narrow band antenna is designed for use in biomedical applications, such as heartbeat and respiratory motion detection. The proposed design is based on the microstrip technology, consisting of 4x4 patch antenna matrix allowing for 17dBi gain. The antenna is simulated using Octave and Open EMS software and the directivity was characterized in an anechoic chamber.

articleTitle: A Hardware Optimized Storage and Retrieval System for Smart Warehousing Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Automated warehouses are widely used in several types of industries. These types of warehouses offer different advantages for the users, from monitoring and control to automated retrieval and organizing of the stored packages. The majority of automated warehouses are much more effective than the classical ones, in which humans manipulate packages. In order to achieve a reduced labor cost and most importantly, to reduce the footprint of the warehouse which can be attained by implementing different types of storage systems, like mobile shelves, shelves on several levels, shelves for pallets, etc. All of the above-mentioned types of structures for deposits can be automated by using robots or different types of package manipulation systems to retrieve and deliver the needed packages. This paper’s purpose is to design and implement a smart storage and retrieval system which manages to reduce the soil footprint of the warehouse to up to 50% in ideal conditions. This is achieved by creating a new type of transportation unit used to retrieve and deliver the packages and by mobilizing the deposits shelf systems. All of these upgrades are all controlled by a single microcontroller with a graphical user interface.

articleTitle: Modified Polynomial Method to Synthesize a Control Algorithm for a System Model with First Order Inertia and Time Delay
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper, it is presented the procedure for synthesis of the control algorithm PI to the model of object with inertia first order and time delay, by the polynomial modified method. In the practice of automation the industrial and technological processes, the slow processes are usually approximated by the mathematical model, that represents the transfer function with inertia first order and time delay. It was elaborated the modified polynomial method for tuning the PI control algorithm to the model of object with inertia first order and time delay, which presents a simple procedure of calculation. To compare the obtained results, the empirical tuning methods, the Ziegler-Nichols method, the maximum stability degree method in analytical form and with iterations, and the parametrical optimization method of tuning the controller are analyzed. It is synthesized the control algorithm by the maximum stability degree method with iterations and polynomial modified method for the two case studies, there are analyzed the obtained results for the case of variation the parameters of the model of object. The advantages of the maximum stability degree method with iterations and modified polynomial method are highlighted.

Author Keywords: model of object with inertia and time delay
the maximum stability degree method with iterations

articleTitle: Experimental measurements of radar absorbing materials in semi anechoic chambers
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper focuses on radar absorbing materials (RAM) characterization simple techniques that can be used in typical semi anechoic chambers for research and development projects. The aim of our work is to evaluate RAM materials performances using common measurement setups available in EMC laboratories. The obtained results made us conclude that further studies may be necessary for conducting more accurate measurements of these materials properties. Anyhow it's possible to use these kind of results in preliminary R&D stages to compare different technologies / project results.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Analysis and Experimental Validation of an IPMSM
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with the electromagnetic analysis of an Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (IPMSM). The study considers the analysis of aspects such as: the cogging torque, the coil-flux linkage, the circuit voltage, and the magnetic flux density in the air gap. Both no-load and rated load operation scenarios were considered. In order to analyze the harmonics for circuit voltage and magnetic flux density in the air gap, a Fourier calculation was implemented. The electromagnetic analysis, performed using JMAG Designer, was validated by experimental study.

articleTitle: On-line monitoring of high power substations - A Romanian experience
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: On-line monitoring and diagnosis of the primary equipment of high voltage electrical substations is generally recognized as necessary and beneficial for power companies, constituting one of the priority actions in developing SMART GRIDS. In Romania, during 2010-2013, CNTEE Transelectrica (the Romanian TSO) implemented a Smart Grid pilot project consisting of the on-line monitoring and diagnosis of all the primary equipment (power transformers, shunt reactors, circuit-breakers, disconnectors, current and voltage transformers, surge arresters) of three high voltage power substations, namely 400/110 kV Darste, 220/110 kV Gradiste and 220/110 kV Mostistea substations., located around the angles of a triangle with about 350 km sides. At the mentioned project pilot were used online monitoring systems of NOVA EMCSIT type, a total of 569 pcs. online monitoring equipment and more than two thousand sensors were used (to which PC servers are added). This paper presents the experience regarding the implementation, operation and efficiency of the monitoring systems in the three mentioned substations. The paper also presents the disturbing factors in the operation of the online monitoring systems and new opportunities for upgrading some of the online monitoring equipment based on the experience gained.

articleTitle: Low frequency magnetic field survey in different areas of a hospital’s environment
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this experimental work we assessed the low-frequency magnetic field strengths in several areas of hospital’s environment: Intensive Care Unit, Orthopedic Surgery Room and Ultrasound Scanner Room. The study referred both to electromagnetic compatibility and electromagnetic biocompatibility issues. The highest value of the magnetic flux density was identified in the ultrasound scanner room, namely 6,985 $\mu$T, near an electromagnetic filter. The recorded values are below 7% of the maximum admissible values according to the ICNIRP, however in all three investigated areas we recorded values above 0,4 $\mu$T, which represents a health risk for long-term exposures, especially for children.

articleTitle: Analysis of the thermal and electrical parameters of the supply system of an HTS superconducting electromagnet
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The proper functioning of a high-temperature superconducting (HTS) electromagnet requests a DC of 300 A supply to obtain a magnetic flux density of 5 T. The current must be applied to the HTS electromagnet through the aid of mixed chain conductors, comprising two types: a copper one and the second, an HTS conductor connected to the magnet. The copper conductor connects the outer terminal on the cryostat to one end of the HTS conductor, having a temperature of 50 K. The second (HTS conductor) has one end at 50 K and the second at 4.2 K, the magnet's temperature. The cooling of the HTS magnet is performed by a Gifford-McMahon cryocooler with two cooling stages: 50 K and 4.2 K. The work aims to design the current conductors and evaluate the heating flux towards the magnet and temperature profile of the system to comply with the cooling power of the cryocooler.

articleTitle: Video Method for Estimating the Apparel Worn Size
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Online commerce has experienced a great opportunity in recent years due to the pandemic. The forecasts show that trends for online purchases are to be maintained, so the competitive challenge consists further in simplifying the interaction with the customer and reducing the time of selecting products. In fashion segment, one of the main factors influencing purchase decision is the certainty of the product fitting on the customer’s size. As solution to this issue, paper presents a video method for determining the size worn in clothes, based on the use of an anatomical reference, the interpupillary distance. The average interpupillary distance in female is 61.63mm and has a standard deviation of 2.66mm and the average interpupillary distance in male is 65.32mm and has a standard deviation of 1.50mm. The method of video estimation of the worn apparel size includes six phases: the identification of the pupils, the determination of the centers of pupils, the calculation of the interpupillary distance in pixels, the video identification of shoulders, the determination of the width of the shoulders in pixels, the conversion of the width of the shoulders in centimeters and determining the size worn.

articleTitle: Python Technology Used For A Human-Machine Interface In Sensors And Transducers Laboratory
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Considering new trends in systems and microsystems to use Open-Source, we realized a graphic user interface (GUI), based on Python technologies, for helping the students to take measurements in the Sensors and transducers laboratory. It is a tool for keeping track of students and grading them using an electronic grid test. The solution presented is to develop a method for monitoring and control of motor speed using a sensory system to take measurements, in the laboratory (on-site). The sensors used are a magnetic encoder, a capacitive proximity sensor, and a stroboscope. Through the electronic grid test, we can evaluate the student’s preliminary knowledge, then, using our GUI, students can manage the measurements automatically: inputs of experimental data, report generation with tables, graphs, and measurement errors. The grades obtained by the students are sent by e-mail, to the teacher, thus easing the routine work.

articleTitle: Opto-Guard: Non-invasive System of Continuous User Assurance of Keeping the Optimal Distance of the Eyes from the Computer Screen
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Computer related health problems, reported to affect up to 90% of users, could be prevented to a very large extent. The knowledge of the risk factors and the timely adoption of measures are exclusively the responsibility of the user, involving a multidirectional approach to mitigate the effects of a prolonged improper position in front of the computer. For this matter, American Optometric Association states that the wrong positioning while performing computer tasks is the major contributing factor to digital screen-related vision problems. As a solution, the paper presents a warden system proposal that uses the computer's web camera to measure the distance at which the user is from its screen. The particularity consists in the video measurement method the system uses, calculating the distance without a reference, increasing the measurement resolution and implicitly the accuracy of the distance measurement. The range of interest for which tests were conducted is between 40 and 63 cm proximity, being the visual depth considered most comfortable. In addition, the system advances a visual warning in the event that the user is not in the visual safety area. The advantage of the Opto-Guard system is that it does not require additional equipment or the user intervention to function, only camera calibration being necessary once.

articleTitle: Improving Online Teaching by Short-Time Activities
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: During the pandemic and the lockdown stage, online teaching based on information and communication technology (ICT) was a challenge for teachers and students. Even if we all have smart devices and Internet access almost everywhere, the problem was the missing feedback of the students, their reduced focusing power and, sometimes, the lack of motivation, even a boring feeling. This research work aims at planning the online teaching based on short time activities with high impact on maintaining the students’ interest in the studied content. Teachers and students must be familiar with the online learning technology. Diversity of the online teaching activities ensures that the students keep their concentration during classes. Competition between students and the possibility of self-evaluation motivate them to perform better and even to be the leader of the group. Time limits for the class activities imposes students to work efficiently and to outdo themselves. Creativity must be encouraged and stimulated by interesting teaching methods. Gaming is a good teaching option for the current and future generations of students as they are so different in comparison to previous other generation. Specially created games can offer the interactive environment for study and teaching. Teachers can use different software tools to develop this kind of activities dedicated to the lecture content. We exemplify some of these activities for online teaching in a Romanian class of Networking and Cybersecurity.

articleTitle: Reliability, Unreliability and Failure Rate of a Hybrid Lighting System
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: As the energy sector is constantly growing in terms of development directions, the reason for analyzing a hybrid system is the fact that it represents a robust, clean and quiet technology with relatively low maintenance costs and a low impact on the environment. The sunlight and wind kinetic energy are free, inexhaustible and do not involve harmful residues or greenhouse gas emissions. The analyzed system is based on the concept of hybrid electricity systems, being an autonomous device designed for street lighting, based on the parallel operation of a wind turbine and a photovoltaic cell system. The Reliability Prediction Mode represents one of the most common forms of analyzing the reliability of a system. This requires the examination of all the parts and components to anticipate their failure rate. Through the reliability prediction method, we evaluate, according to the characteristics taken from the manufacturer’s technical sheet, if the analyzed system works in a normal operating environment for a period of 30000 hours. This system takes into consideration the natural compensation of solar and wind potential, thus, the parallel operation of these two energy conversion systems allows to obtain and increased safety in power supply and achieve yields superior to their separate functioning. The study focuses on obtaining results on the reliability of a hybrid system developed for street lighting by calculating three essential indicators that show if the system’s performance is reliable over a period of 30000 hours of operation, subsequently allowing us to determine if indeed, it is a profitable investment against a traditional street lighting system.

articleTitle: The shielding performance analysis for different types of composite materials
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents aspects related to the electromagnetic shielding materials used in the construction of various types of specialized electromagnetic field (EMC) test site. Important aspects of the machine process and how to make the electromagnetic shield are also presented. Five different types of composite materials are presented from the point of view of their structure. They have been tested according to the specific standard IEEE Std 299:2006. The shielding effectiveness of the five different types of architectural shielding materials was calculated for each material separately, and then compared. The tabular presentation of the results was made in order to compare the effectiveness of the screening they have. Conclusions regarding the shielding performances that each analyzed material recorded during the measurements performed are also presented.

articleTitle: The Angular Sensitivity Characteristic of a Photometer – an Ignored Parameter
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The angular sensitivity characteristic of a photometer is an important parameter when measuring illumination, but in many other situations it is less important, such as measuring luminance, where the incidence of light is normal. The starting point of the research is the finding that there are many situations in which this parameter is neglected, although it should not be. The angular sensitivity can generate errors when measuring illumination, but also in many other configurations where direct or indirect lighting measurements are involved, also for Light Field Analysis, for tracking the angular position, for automatic adjustment of indoor lighting, or even in the case of Visible-Light Positioning Systems. Some such examples from the literature are analyzed to demonstrate this. The experimental approach is based on a goniometric stand, with the help of which angular sensitivity characteristics of some sensors and photometers used in current practice is determined, also following the possibility of compensating cosine errors. The conclusions represent a clearer picture of how this type of error manifests in lighting engineering measurements.

articleTitle: Reliability estimation for smart metering units in a Energy Distribution Branch with prosumers
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Currently, in the electricity distribution subsidiaries, a special emphasis is placed on reducing the operating costs of measuring and protection equipment. Thus, it is necessary to determine with high precision the devices that have malfunctions and need to be replaced within a certain time interval. The current work aims to develop an algorithm for the automatic identification of these equipment, based on reliability and maintenance indicators, as well as external factors. The proposed algorithm is built on the basis of a non-linear optimization function in which internal variables (provided by the equipment manufacturer) as well as external variables (unpredictable events such as: climatic factors, atmospheric overvoltages, mechanical damage, etc.) intervene and on the basis of some restrictions imposed by the operator distribution in order to reduce energy losses as well as from the point of view of protecting the equipment.

articleTitle: Obtaining Nanocomposite Films With Predefined Thermal Conductivity, With Controlled Anisotropy
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article presents a new concept of nanocomposite film type materials with predefined thermal anisotropy, of high value, controlled by a compositing technology with exposure to electromagnetic radiation, with a high degree of innovation. The proposed technology is in line with the new concepts of cooling at the micro-scale, and can lead to materials made at the micro/nanometric scale and innovative technologies mainly oriented towards the electronic, bio-medical and aeronautical industries.

Author Keywords: films with pre-defined anisotropic thermal conductivity
orientation and stabilization of nanoparticles in the electromagnetic field

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Five-Level Reduced Switch Inverter Based Bidirectional Isolated DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper addresses the modeling and analysis of a new bidirectional isolated dc-dc converter (BIDC) based on a multilevel inverter topology. The novelty of the study is the utilization of the reduced switch five-level inverter topology instead of the conventional full-bridge dual active bridge. It has the advantage of lower voltage/current stress on the switches at higher voltages as compared to traditional BIDCs. Power transfer between primary and secondary sides is controlled by PI controller-based single phase shift (SPS) modulation technique. The proposed converter stands out for having: i) employing a reduced number of switches compared to other multilevel inverter-based bidirectional dc-dc converter topologies ii) high voltage gain iii) low harmonic level iv) suitable for integrating multiple input multiple output electrical systems and to be used in bipolar dc microgrid applications. In order to validate the performance of the proposed converter, a simulation model has been developed in Matlab/Simulink environment. The performance of the suggested converter and the controller scheme under steady-state and dynamic conditions have been revealed through the simulation results.

articleTitle: Implementation of a remote controlled photovoltaic nano-grid
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a solution in the context of Home Energy Management Systems (HEMS) and a practical implementation of a remotely controlled nano-grid structure. The novelty of the subject consists in the improvements on the ease of access and control of the implied equipment, with issues of reconfiguration and integration of open-source software. The proposed configuration allows real-time control and monitoring of the devices and their parameters and the global grid electrical energy parameters for the produced and consumed power. This system also gives the possibility of power consumption monitoring, forecasting and prediction at specific preset period. The system can also monitor and record the average operating time, the average load level of the grid, and other details about the past or future behavior of the equipment plus different quality or statistic energy quality indicators such as energy transfer efficiency.

articleTitle: Dielectric parameters of circulating tumor cells – in search of the most suitable buffer solution
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Background: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs), a potential biomarker for cancer diagnosis and treatment monitoring, are characterized by high heterogeneity and scarcity in peripheral blood, making them difficult to be detected by conventional laboratory methods. In this context, the use of alternative methods such as dielectrophoresis and broadband dielectric spectroscopy as complementary tools for CTCs detection is of great interest. One first methodological issue related to the abovementioned techniques is related to choosing the optimal buffer solution, as the buffer can have a negative impact on CTCs fragility and electrode polarization. Thus, the aim of this study is to determine the optimal buffer solution when measuring the dielectric parameters of CTCs.Materials and method: Three commonly used sucrose-base buffers were tested. The dielectric measurements were conducted using the Novocontrol Alpha A Analyzer and the BDS 1200 sample measuring cell. We determine the dielectric properties of the solutions without and with suspended THP-1 cells. Subsequently, equivalent Randles electrical circuits were designed.Results: An impedance decrease of at least 40% over the frequency range from 10 Hz to 5000 Hz and a significant increase of the phase angle for the 200Hz domain were observed in sucrose + HEPES solution when THP-1 cells were added, while no changes were encountered in the other buffers.Conclusion: Sucrose + HEPES solution was the most suitable buffer for this kind of experiment. The article highlights the importance of choosing the appropriate buffer for dielectric measurements of CTCs, demonstrating the method’s feasibility for clinical use.

articleTitle: ISense - Parkinson's symptoms monitoring module based on inertial measuring units sensors
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper, there is an analysis of what a system that detected Parkinson-like behavior should be structured like; the system should keep as key attributes ease of use and long-term analysis. The module in the ISense system for the monitoring of movements specific to Parkinson's disease aims to constantly detect and analyze the movements specific to this condition made by a subject, in order to determine from an early stage whether he suffers from Parkinson’s and how the disease manifests itself. Several methods of diagnosing Parkinson's disease by detecting specific tremor have been identified in the specialized literature.

articleTitle: Assessment of HV Power Supply Efficiency in Plasma Activated Water Production
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Plasma-liquid interactions are becoming an increasingly significant topic in the field of plasma technology. The interaction of non-equilibrium plasma with a liquid state is used in many applications such as surface treatment, health care, water purification, decontamination of foods and agricultural applications. Recently, numerous studies have reported that plasma-activated water has the ability to improve plant germination and growth due to the reactive oxygen and nitrogen species produced in it. This paper presents the energy efficiency of generating hydrogen peroxide concentration in plasma activated water. A non-thermal T-shaped plasma spray system at atmospheric pressure in argon is used which is supplied with energy from two high voltage sources: an AC source and a DC pulse power supply. A digital diaphragm pump is used to inject water at different flow rates, keeping the argon flow rate constant.

articleTitle: A non-enzymatic chronoamperometric glucose sensor based on Screen-Printed Carbon Electrode (SPCE) modified with maghemite magnetic nanoparticles via physical vapour deposition (PVD)
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Early diagnosis of many severe diseases such as diabetes, nerve degeneration, and cardiovascular diseases requires the detection of glucose levels in the human body. A non-enzymatic sensor was developed via screen-printing to obtain a screen-printed carbon electrode that was modified with magnetic maghemite nanoparticles via physical vapor deposition, to enhance the affinity of the sensor towards glucose detection, using chronoamperometry as an electrochemical detection method.

articleTitle: Continuous Improvement in Education Based on Deming Model in Worldwide Context
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to make a brief comparative study between online vs onsite education and to improve existing learning formats and educational technologies using Deming Model in such a way to increase presence at laboratory and grades of the students at exam. This study was done for students in first year at electromagnetic theory laboratory. For this study we will take into account like inputs the learning methods used and like outputs the student’s presence, grades obtain by students and feedback offer by students to the teacher. This study was performed in the last 2 years, where the classes for year 2020-2021 was done online and for 2021-2022 onsite. This study can also decrease the dropout rate in university by making the laboratories more attractive for students.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Performances of Battery Electric Vehicles Using ADVISOR
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper addresses issues related to the performances of battery electric vehicle. To perform the study, the authors used the ADVISOR (Advanced Vehicle Simulator) software, running under MATLAB/Simulink. The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) together with the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) and industry partners developed this software, to make an easy-using tool but also sophisticated and with various possibilities to conFigure a certain type of vehicle. Now, the software allows simulating all types of vehicles: classical with internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles, hybrid (series or parallel), pure electric or fuel cell vehicles. During the paper, the authors explain aspects of the vehicle type configuration, the possibilities of changing the components or the control logic of the vehicle, as well as the simulation results and their significance.

articleTitle: Improvement of adaptive single-phase automatic reclosing in extra-high voltage lines
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article deals with the issue of improving the adaptive single-phase automatic reclosing in extra-high voltage lines. The adaptive single-phase automatic reclosing devices developed in our country and abroad reduce the probability of switching on a phase at the final stage of the single-phase automatic reclosing to an unresolved single-phase short circuit or a re-arising arc, but do not completely exclude such a situation. A method is proposed in which, by preliminary calculations of the currents of the emergency phase, two zones adjacent to the systems are determined on the line, and a short-term one-sided switching on/off the emergency phase is carried out from the side of system 1, if a short or arc fault is detected in the second zone adjacent to system 2, and accordingly one-sided closing of the emergency phase from system 2, if a fault is detected in zone 1 adjacent to system 1. The proposed method for improving the adaptive single-phase automatic reclosing makes it possible to reliably identify a single-phase short or arc fault in 500 and 750 kV extra-high voltage lines with their length in the range 300 - 600 km. An example of calculating the zone boundary on a 500 kV line 500 km long is given, the necessary settings for reliable damage identification are determined.

Author Keywords: successful one way closing of the emergency phase
unsuccessful one way closing of the emergency phase

articleTitle: Portable Device for Measuring Lighting Characteristics in Working Spaces
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Knowing the characteristics of the lighting system in a working place is important as numerous studies have shown that the quality of light can influence the mood and productivity of people working in those spaces. This research proposes the creation of a portable device that can be used to measure characteristics of lighting systems in working places. The device is based on TCS34725 light sensors and is used to measure, in an automatic way, different light parameters. The paper presents an initial prototype of the device which includes a microcontroller board, light sensors, a step motor, a step motor drive and a Bluetooth (BT) module. Using the BT connection, the device can be controlled remotely using a smartphone, the data can be transmitted and recorded on the smartphone or can be sent to the cloud for storing and processing.

articleTitle: Measurement and Numerical Simulation of the Low-Frequency Electric Field Generated by an Overhead Power Line
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this study, the low-frequency electric field generated by a 110-kV double-circuit overhead power line is comparatively assessed by measurements and numerical simulations. Measurements were performed with a selfdeveloped 5 Hz – 2 kHz electric field sensor (EFS-01) in conjunction with a portable signal analyzing device, i.e. Fluke 43 single-phase power quality analyzer, while simulations were performed using a 2D finite element model developed in ANSYS Maxwell 2D. The results obtained by the two methods are in good agreement and in line with expected exposure field levels for such types of 110-kV overhead power lines.

articleTitle: Building Services Engineering in the Assessment Process for European Energy Award
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: European Energy Award - EEA is a voluntary quality management and award system which supports local authorities in Europe and implicitly Romania by establishing approaches to interdisciplinary planning and implementation if effective energy and climate policy. The standardized evaluation procedure allows performance comparison of the different communities that are interested in obtaining the title of sustainable community. In Romania the city that pass the assessment receive are called „Comunitate Sustenabila EEA“. EEA is an instrument qualified for management of energy policy which allows municipalities to identify strengths, weaknesses, and potential for improvement, but above all to implement energy efficient strategies. All these efforts are visible through a standardized assessment that allows us to observe the differences between municipalities involved in EEA. The EEA project has a close connection with the building services engineer field because in each of the 6 areas there are measures related to this field. In some areas such as Supply & disposal or Municipal buildings & facilities, the building services engineer domain holds over 80% of the measures.

articleTitle: Gait Rehabilitation in Virtual Reality Serious Game Interactive Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Fall accidents are generally very harmful and can be the consequence of gait impairments, that’s why it’s very important for a person to have regular checkups if they notice any unusual differences in the way they use to walk. The way a person walks can at times be characterized by a certain anomaly that can compromise their everyday routines and be an enormous risk to their state of health. These types of anomalies are known as Gait disorders. Inside the healthcare areas of physiotherapy and rehabilitation, the growing demand to improve the quality and efficiency of treatments, has led to several experimentations, developments, and implementations of various types of technologies and innovations in the past few years, to allow patients with these types of conditions to reach a faster and more motivating recovery. In this paper is presented a solution designed and implemented to be used for gait based on the concept of 3D serious games. Virtual reality interactive scenarios were considered and implemented using the software platform Unity 3D and the interaction between the user and the VR scenario is carried out by Azure Kinect. Microsoft Azure Kinect SDK is used to extract the body joints tracking. The proposed solution includes a Web application designed for physiotherapists to access the electronic health record of their patients but also to prescribe the training plan supported by the high interactive VR scenarios of the proposed serious game. Based on the joins acquired data different metrics are considered and used to validate the capabilities of proposed system.

articleTitle: Application For Processing Non-electric Biological Signals
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents a series of obtained results regarding the signal processing of non-electrical biological signals. To implement an application that helps people who specialize in the interpretation of entered data, such as the security of medical data. A well-known and difficult to interpret example is the respiratory signal, which is not associated with variations in electrical voltage. Therefore, with the help of some transducers, the electrical signal is associated with the respiratory signal, which can be affected by noise. The presence of these noises can be corrected by using high-performance filters, such as digital filters. A graphical interface has been developed in MATLAB 2021B for digital filtering of these signals. All necessary filtering functions have been introduced. For a user-friendly design, App Designer was used, an interactive development environment for designing programming applications that have a number of well-established functions. Programming was done using the MATLAB editor. By means of the predefined buttons the user can load the raw biological signals or choose the desired filter. At the same time, different digital filters have been implemented that can be selected from the interface: Butterworth, High pass, Low pass or Notch. To validate the filtering results, the publicly available database “ICBHI 2017 Challenge” has been accessed. Be a complex field that requires knowledge of electrical engineering and medical bioengineering to be understood and treated correctly.

articleTitle: Controlled Switching Taking Into Account the Standard Deviation of Switching Time
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The controlled switching of electrical equipment is a vast field analyzed in the literature. In practice, switching times of electrical equipment vary depending on several parameters (type of energy accumulation, ambient temperature, number of actuations, duration since last actuation, etc.) These disturbances can lead to the creation of a very disruptive transient regime, switching at a time that deviates from the optimal point. The greater the deviation, the more disruptive the transient regime produced. In this paper, the impact of the deviation of the moment of connection from the optimal moment is analyzed, in case of connecting the various equipment in the electrical system.

articleTitle: Case Studies Related to the Optimization of a Surface Mounted Permanent Magnets Synchronous Generator Applied for a Small Hydrokinetic Turbine
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Cogging torque mitigation is the main objective of several studies concerning the optimization of surface mounted permanent magnets synchronous generator (SMPMSG). This paper is presenting two optimization techniques implemented through finite element method and some experimental results for a horizontal axis hydrokinetic turbine. The two optimizations consist in, the adaptation of the radial angle between the magnets and the axial skewing of the magnets. The optimizations are performed using co-simulation between Altair HyperStudy and Flux software packages, using the Global Response Search Method. Experiments with the 0.5 kVA generator’s prototype presented with the findings supported by the measurements. Also, the unbalanced force that acts on the rotor has been analyzed for the initial model and optimized ones, that have a nonsymmetrical magnetic field in the airgap.

articleTitle: hBag - Smart Assistant for Healthy Shopping
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents a method of improving the quality of consumption of different products, through a mobile application build for Android operating system. It is a smart assistant for shopping management, because it can help a user to choose the optimal product for him. When scanning a product barcode, the user can see the details of this product, like the quality of ingredients or the brand. This app was developed using java programming language, with Spring Framework and its libraries.

articleTitle: Direct Current Motor Speed Adjustment Via Indirect Self-Adjusting Regulator
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper are approached aspects related to the adjustment of the d.c. motor speed, by means of the indirect self-tuning regulator. Constructive and functional features of self-tuning adaptive regulators are specified. Reference is made to the explicit and implicit combinations of the estimation and design methods of the regulator. Elements regarding the initialization, supervision and implementation of self-tuning regulators are highlighted.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of metaheuristic algorithms for optimal reactive power control in microgrids
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: As power systems are evolving towards a decentralized model, entities such as microgrid are increasing in popularity. The reactive power control has a major role in improving the microgrid operational conditions. In this paper, five different metaheuristic algorithms are applied for determining the optimal reactive power control for a medium voltage microgrid integrating photovoltaic power plants and capacitor banks. The main purpose of this paper is to conduct a performance analysis for the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), Salp Swarm Optimizer (SSA), Sine-Cosine Algorithm (SCA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Genetic Algorithm (GA). The results reveal that the GWO is the most performant algorithm, followed by the SSA and PSO, while the SCA and GA obtained the lowest performance.

articleTitle: The Influence of TCSC Devices on Distance Protection Tripping Characteristic
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The Thyristor Controlled Series Compensator is part of the Flexible AC Transmission System device category that uses series compensation to regulate active and reactive power flows. This device changes its impedance value depending on the firing angle of its two thyristors placed in antiparallel. The distance protection has the role oflocating the short-circuits present on the line, by measuring the impedance at one of the ends of the line and of trip the circuit breaker with a delay depending on the distance to the short-circuit. The paper highlights some problems that may appear in the correct functioning of the distance protection, due to the change in the impedance of the network. Also, the strengths and weaknesses of the main types of operating characteristics are presented.

articleTitle: Analysis and Optimal Design of a Wireless Power Transfer System for Electrical Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The increase of electrical vehicles market led to the increase of the interest regarding development of their battery charging techniques. Thus, the wireless power transfer technology based on the inductive power transfer becomes more and more attractive and highly used in charging electrical vehicles since is a safe, flexible, and a modern technique, which doesn’t imply connecting a feeding cable, the energy transfer beginning after the receiver and emitter alignment. In this light, the present paper proposes the design of a wireless power transfer system for the electrical vehicles and its analysis, through numerical modelling, in order to determine an optimum structure of high energy efficiency. Throughout the analysis, the determination of the coupling coefficient and the electrical parameters specific to the system depending on the number of ferrite bars, which is considered to be part of the bipolar pads of the system is followed, depending on the distance between the transmitter and receiver and the size of the coils that form the system. These studies take into consideration the magnetic field distributions which also influence the coupling coefficient, and finally offer an optimum structure of the wireless power transfer system for electrical vehicles.

articleTitle: Modelling and Simulation of Virtual Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper proposes a simulation model of Virtual Power Plants (VPP) and analysis the impact of the proposed model in frequency control. This paper, also, analyses the impact of reduced inertia on the hydro power plants stability. The simulations were done considering an increased share of renewable energy sources (RES) in electrical power production and a reduction of system inertia. The simulations were performed in Matlab/Simulink on the Kundur two-area frequency model which contains both primary and secondary frequency control levels. The simulation time was considered equal to 900 seconds, equivalent to 15 minutes, this being a reference value for secondary frequency control. The virtual power plant is composed of hydro power plants, renewable sources and energy storage systems and is controlled by a hybrid controller meaning that the VPP can contribute to both primary and secondary frequency control.

articleTitle: Piezoelectric Nanofibrous Composite Materials for Energy and Electronic Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper discusses the development of composite materials with a piezoelectric effect. Polymeric mats of different shapes were made from electrospun piezoelectric nanofibers, and the piezo effect was improved by adjusting the electrospinning device in order to increase the electric field between the electrodes at the time of dipolar polarization. The electromechanical response of the resulting composite materials, which are made up of the mats and a silicon rubber matrix, is then assessed. By appropriately integrating the nanofibers into the host material, as shown by images obtained using electron microscopy, delaminations, that might have occurred with piezoelectric films, are avoided. Last but not least, it has been demonstrated that both vibration and impact stimuli result in a sizable electrical reaction.

articleTitle: Analytical Performance Investigation of a Commercial Solar Air Heater
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents the results of analytical modeling and simulation of the performance of a commercial air heating solar panel with the help of the MATLAB software environment. They are presented in terms of plotted graphs generated on the basis of characteristic functions of the considered solar system. The gathered data through the implied software environment are compared with real values acquired with the help of a pyranometer, one humidity sensor, two thermocouple sensors type J, four signal adapters and a module that offers the possibility of data recording. The comparation of the analytical model with an experimental model is useful to eventually validate the simulation model.

articleTitle: Foundation Structural Resistance Calculation of SF6 High-Voltage Circuit Breaker
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents how is performed a foundation structural resistance calculation of SF6 high-voltage circuit breaker. The foundation represents the lower part of a building that has the role of transmitting the loads from the superstructure to the foundation ground and of participating, along with the other structural elements, in ensuring the strength, stability, exploitation and durability of the construction. For the structural design the type of foundation is chosen, the height of the foundation and the reinforcement of the concrete elements are established. The article also illustrates how the mechanical vibrations can affect the good exploit of the high-voltage circuit breaker due to foundation structural resistance problem.

articleTitle: Influence of Household Tools in Regional Configuration of Earthquake Early Warning Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Tectonic activity can't be foreseen in time, therefore its occurrence causes every time human and economic losses. So far it has not been identified any solid method to forecast an earthquake instance. At the moment there are only methods for quick notification, send after the occurrence of the event, running the Earthquake Early Warning Systems (EEWS). Their main purpose is to disseminate the information about potentially catastrophic hazards as early is possible to vulnerable people in the targeted area, to provide enough time to implement automatized emergency measures. The warning is possible due to the fact that the onset of the earthquake is carried out by non-destructive primary P waves propagating with high speed. Performance of EEWS detection is given by technical characteristics and also by external natural factors, as changing sites’ configuration or parasitic signals that can interfere. In this context, the paper aims to demonstrate that there can be an overlap, an interval of confusion of the signals that EEWS can perceive and interpret as announcing natural catastrophes. There were tested eight heavy tools commonly used in household and their predominant frequency was calculated and compared to recorded seismic predominant frequencies. If the alert threshold level is set for 1Hz, it can trigger as well for heavy tools vibrations as for low intensity earthquakes.

articleTitle: Preliminary Model of a Method for Selectively Switch Controllable Voltage Sources in Power Supply Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents a solution that relates to a method for the selective switching (connection/disconnection) of voltage sources and/or of converter modules controllable and connected in parallel in the composition of power supply systems, which involves events whose transition is modeled in a specific manner. Its mathematical model is validated by analytical results (MATLAB & Simulink) and by experimental results (dSPACE DS1103).

articleTitle: Influence of MV Networks’ Distributed Neutral Grounding on the Homopolar Directional Current Protection
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper aims to establish the influence of the distributed treatment of the neutral in the MV networks on the operation of the power lines affected by single-phase faults and the current protection system of the entire affected network. At the same time, part of the technical conditions that must be met by the distributed treatment coil are established so that the protections specific to the single-phase fault work safely and selectively, and as a result, do not worsen the continuity indicators in the electricity supply of the users.

articleTitle: The Influence of Electrical Equipment Structural Elements on their Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents a review of the main obstacle that occurs in electrical equipment wireless communication networks. Wireless communications represent one of the biggest advantages in today's technology evolution. Remote access to the monitoring of electrical equipment is a necessity nowadays. All wireless connectivity devices are susceptible to wireless interference, communication devices within electrical equipment are no exception. There are many obstacles in the construction of power management equipment and buildings that can interfere with wireless communication signals. However, often the building elements of electrical equipment are more difficult to replace. The paper proposes a presentation of the main types of obstacles known in wireless communications. Also, it was proposed solutions to diminish the influences on the wireless communication network, in order to avoid operation malfunction of the electrical equipment.

articleTitle: Influence of Water Injection Technique in an Argon NTP System Used for PAW Generation
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Non-thermal plasma technologies, considered innovative and environmentally friendly, have an important role on applications in diverse fields including agriculture, biomedicine, food packaging and surface treatment. This paper presents an analysis of the influence of different parameters on the energy efficiency of a T-shaped non-thermal plasma system at atmospheric pressure for plasma activated water generation. For this purpose, a high voltage AC source was used which consisted of a zero voltage switching flyback converter of 25 kHz. Demineralized water was injected into the system at different flow rates (10, 20, 30mL/min) via two different water pumps, one pumping water continuously and one in pulse, keeping the argon flow rate constant at 1 L/min. To compare the energy efficiency of the power supply for the two types of water sources, the hydrogen peroxide concentration of the plasma-activated water was measured.

articleTitle: Analysis and Practical Implementation of an Independent Double Buck Interleaved Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents and analyzes the operation of a patented bidirectional dc-dc converter power stage topology, working in step-down (buck) mode. The structure of the proposed and analyzed step-down dc-dc converter is called “Independent Double Buck Interleaved Converter (IDbIC).’' The study of the investigated power stage structure was conducted both theoretical and experimental. Theoretical study stage includes the following objectives: presentation of the dc-dc converter power stage, development of a mathematical model for continuous conduction mode (CCM) of the IDbIC, and the implementation of a simulation and validation model for the results obtained in the mathematical - analytical model. Also, within the experimental study, a physical model of the proposed power stage converter was developed. On the same prototype, the functionality of the IDbIC converter structure was validated. Moreover, using the experimental prototype, the power stage efficiency of the proposed dc-dc converter, was determined at various levels of input voltage and output power.

articleTitle: Automatic Gait Analysis and Classification in Video Sequences
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Gait abnormalities can be related to locomotion injuries or to various musculoskeletal and neurological pathologies. In this paper an automatic method for gait analysis and evaluation is proposed. It can be used for rehabilitation assessment but also to detect the gait abnormalities. The proposed system is noninvasive and it is based on the analysis of the video sequences captured in the sagittal plane. The MoveNet pose estimation model is used to detect the joints positions of the body segments. Then the knee and thigh-trunk angles on both left and right side are computed in each frame of the video sequence to study their variation. The video sequences can have different lengths and frame rates, therefore the analysis will be done at stride level by using statistical parameters. Experiments were made on a reduced number of video sequences that contain pathological gait and normal gait. Data augmentation was applied to increase the volume of data which is then used for gait classification.

articleTitle: Monitoring and Diagnosis of Electrical Equipment by Infrared Thermography
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper aims to present the procedure applied to the monitoring and diagnosis of thermal stresses of electrical equipment by means of infrared technique. A case study is presented with an analysis of an event identified by infrared thermography. The warmer the body in question, the higher the energy emitted in the form of infrared radiation. Basically, infrared (IR) thermography also allows us to see what we cannot normally see with the naked eye. Infrared thermographic cameras allow viewing the thermal spectrum and identifying problems by quantifying them in a non-contact measurement and presenting the results obtained in the form of technical reports. If either faulty electrical equipment or unsuitable electrical charging conditions, or damaged metal or non-metallic components are encountered, they are usually due to abnormal temperature patterns that can be highlighted by infrared thermographic cameras. Monitoring and diagnosing the thermal stresses of electrical equipment by infrared thermography is one of the most common methods currently applied in transformer substations.

articleTitle: Clustering-Using Data Mining-based Application to Identify the Hourly Loading Patterns of the Generation Units from the Hydropower Plants
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The proper operation of a hydropower plant (HPP) imposes the collection and processing of a huge amount of input data to establish the optimal regimes subject to the technical and economic constraints. In the context in which the strategies applied in the HPP by the Decision-Makers (DMs) do not include the techniques to work with the large database and extract information for the short time horizons, a clustering-using Data Mining-based application has been proposed in the paper to obtain the hourly loading patterns of the generation units. They are used in the daily generation scheduling, considering a rule-based procedure to make the decision process more efficient with the benefits of the energy production and predictive maintenance plans at the level of the equipment/installations. The application has been tested considering the hourly records saved in the database of the SCADA system integrated into an HPP with six generation units belonging to the hydro arrangement of the main river in eastern Romania from the year 2019. The optimal solution associated with a quality partition formed by 25 patterns has been obtained using the k-means clustering algorithm considering an internal evaluation indicator, namely Silhouette Coefficient. Knowing these patterns, the DM can load the generation units such that an optimal operation to characterize the HPP.

articleTitle: Optimal Reactive Power Dispatch Considering Load Variation in Distribution Networks using an Improved Sine-Cosine Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The accelerated economic development during the latest decades resulted in an increased electricity demand around the world and major challenges for power systems. Moreover, the climate changes mitigation measures triggered significant changes and an increased pressure on all power systems sectors from generation to distribution and consumers. The Optimal Reactive Power Dispatch (ORPD) is a key component for reducing the active power losses and improving the bus voltage profiles in distribution networks. In this paper, an Improved Sine-Cosine Algorithm (ImSCA) is proposed for solving the ORPD for a distribution network operating under different load scenarios. The case study presents a performance comparison between the proposed ImSCA and the classical Sine-Cosine Algorithm (SCA) and the reactive power control impact upon the network operational conditions.

articleTitle: Challenges and Opportunities of Agri-PV systems in a Clean Energy Transition for Rural Areas
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: A powerful conceptual element in a clean energy transition vision to achieve climate neutrality by 2050 is presented by the development of Agri-PV systems, which have the potential to provide a deep transformation of the agricultural sector. The paper presents an analysis of some of the most important challenges of Agri-PV systems as well as its advantages to make the agricultural sector more resilient and to support delivery of sustainable energy and food all over the world.

articleTitle: Solutions for Digital Interaction of a Resilient Energy Community in a Service-oriented Framework
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Energy communities are emerging entities which need their own Information and Communication System. Resilience is a key metric of such communities, and it has to be implemented for both energy supply versus public network outages and for its information system versus cyber-attacks, acting as cyber-citadels which have to resist external malicious attacks while having also digital interactions with external entities. The paper presents solutions for a resilient energy community with appropriate implementations of digital interaction for data exchange, in order to acquire external energy service for specialized companies and to deliver also information and communication-related services for external users. Principles of a Contractual Data Protection Regulation are presented, as an adaptation of data protection tailored for automated energy services and based on secure data exchange. The principles are verified in a demonstration project which has also external entities with digital interaction.

articleTitle: Electricity losses optimization in distribution networks from the perspective of integration on large scale of renewable energy resources
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper aims to present essential aspects in ensuring the operation in optimal quality conditions of the electricity distribution systems from the point of view of the stability of the supply voltage, the resilience of the distribution systems in the face of natural disasters, increasingly present in the recent period, through the use of NWA, non-wires alternatives technologies. The paper ends with a case study in which a network area is presented, in real mode, to which a series of prosumers have been aggregated showing the power flow in certain hours of the day and the energy losses in the presence of distributed generation, respectively in its absence.

articleTitle: The influence of VSC - HVDC links on AC networks. Mathematical modeling and analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The current article is an analysis of the impact made by the implementation of a VSC – HVDC link within a Test Network, using SmartFlow/EUROSTAG softwares. Different operating scenarios will be analyzed from the point of view of the steady state regime: influence on power flows, N elements regime and contingency regime with N-1 elements, and also the impact over the power losses at the level of the analyzed AC network. To support this detailed analysis, the article also contains a synthesized presentation of the mathematical model that is the basis of modeling VSC-HVDC links in steady state and dynamic regimes.The conclusions of the article highlights the main advantages brought by the consideration of DC (Direct Current) links within modern AC networks, especially in the context of the Romanian National Electric Power System, where there is a tendency in renewable sources integration, which will lead to special requirements, in order to avoid system congestions, such as longer distances links, and additional support in the dynamic stability of the system.

articleTitle: Prosumer Concept Considering the Building Energy Efficiency Situation
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The way in which energy can be produced, stored, distributed and consumed as economically as possible, without making waste, is a problem that has started to be taken seriously by more and more countries in recent years, taking into consideration global warming, the accelerated population growth, industrialization as well as the geopolitical situation. This paper focuses on the production, storage and consumption of energy in an independent manner, without the involvement of the grid, by using the solar energy. Accordingly are presented from the main global policies in the fight for the energy efficiency of buildings, the concept of occupant thermal comfort, up to the integration of BEMS and IoT on buildings. It has been shown through a case study that had as its subject an existing residential building located in an area where the continuity of the electricity supply from the grid is constantly affected, that energy independence can be achieved and even the remaining can be delivered to the grid, thus becoming prosumer, by implementing a solar system with storage units.

articleTitle: Fault Detection Device for PV Array using the Page-Hinkley Test
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In a system of solar energy production, defects can cause a partial or total loss of energy, damage to the system, or failure to safety. Detecting defects is more than necessary to ensure reliability, productivity, safety, and system efficiency. In this paper, we propose a device appropriate for fault detection on the PV plant such as shading. The Bishop model is adapted to the defaults studied in such a system because it considers the avalanche mode of a cell. The model is used to estimate the output values of the system including current, voltage, and power based on the measured inputs such as temperature and irradiance. The model is implemented in the programmable card-based device. Afterward, the residues calculated from the difference between the estimated and the measured value are used in the detection algorithm. Then the Page-Hinkley algorithm is implemented in the card to verify any eventual mean jumps of the residues. The interest of the device is to offer a low-cost monitoring system able to detect any defects in the PV system. The device was tested on the photovoltaic system installed at the Vignola-Ajaccio site to confirm its performance.

articleTitle: The Use of Thévenin, Norton and Hybrid Equivalent Circuits in The Analysis and Polarization of Nonlinear Analog Circuits
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The main goal of this paper is to clearly and correctly define circuits that allow the segregation of linear portions of the electronic circuits from nonlinear ones and in this manner the polarization process of the electronic devices becomes more efficient. These circuits will be further on called hybrid equivalent circuits. When a circuit having a small number of nonlinear and linear circuit elements, nonlinear components are being analyzed, the analysis itself, synthesis and its simulation becomes more efficient if nonlinear side of the circuit is segregated from the linear side. This paper proposes a new modeling technique, called $H \sim$ -modeling, introduced for multi-port networks analysis. It will be further on presented and described that $H \sim$ models are more dynamic and able to describe port behavior more accurately, compared to Thevenin or Norton equivalent circuits. A particular type of model $H \sim$ it is as well presented, called model $H \sim$ nullified, or simply model $H \sim$; and many of its modeling properties are investigated, including circuit energy management. It is demonstrated that the H models are not limited to single-port networks, but also cover multiport. A key characteristic of H modeling is the local polarization of transistors and the segregation of nonlinear components from the linear ones for a faster and more efficient polarization of the circuit. This develops opportunities for circuits developers to benefit of H-modeling and bias individual transistors (or in combinations) without having to execute the normal circuit biasing. The segregation of linear from nonlinear portions of the analog circuit is being proposed as a main strategy in order to gain full control of the nonlinear portions or components. This segregation is actually being achieved by introducing a new port model that nullifies the nonlinear ports of circuits. At the end, leading to a new polarizing technique for nonlinear components.

articleTitle: Web-Application for Assisting Solar Storage Design
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The starting point of this paper is based on the need to design energy storage systems as correctly as possible, given that renewable energy sources, characterized by unpredictability and instability, will represent 57% of the world’s electricity production in the very next 10 years. Any large scale photovoltaic or wind power plant project must also contain a distinct part of a properly sized storage system. For the concrete case of Romania, are analyzed the seasonality index and practical potential (averaged over the entire surface of the country). These parameters influence the amount of electricity that can be produced by a certain photovoltaic plant within a year, including from the perspective of designing a system of adjacent storage. Then, for a certain geographical location, other four complementary parameters are customized and analyzed in detail. They all together provide essential information regarding the worst cases of solar illumination, for a certain number of consecutive days and for each month of the year. The calculation of these parameters was possible using the data made available by the open-source platform of the Power project supported by NASA. It is presented how to use this online tool, very functional for any calculation of electrical energy storage systems intended to ensure the autonomous operation of a photovoltaic plant not connected to the power grid. The results of the calculation of these four parameters associated with four representative locations in Romania are presented. These outputs can be displayed in graphical or tabular form. At the end there are presented considerations and comments regarding the interpretation, comparison and use of this data.

articleTitle: Extending the Life of Transformer Units Through Maintenance Based on Insulation Revitalization
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Globally, lately there has been the issue of efficient maintenance of equipment in energy systems through continuous monitoring and diagnosis. This paper presents a solution/ method that facilitates the achievement of an optimal maintenance for high power transformers, which leads to the prolongation of their life and implicitly to safe and reliable operation. Humidity is considered the biggest enemy of transformer insulation, starting from this premise, the authors have the advantages of using a method of dehumidification of oil-paper insulation with zeolite molecular sieves. The method was applied on transformers in operation, and the results obtained are positive, the use of the installation led to an increase in service life.

articleTitle: Electrical Fault Detection for Industry 4.0 using Fusion deep Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper, problems found in electrical power transmission lines are looked into and put into groups with the help of artificial neural networks. An idea is floating around for a method that uses the three-phase currents and the voltage at one end as inputs. In this process, both the feedforward neural network and the back propagation method are used. Both approaches have the ability to find errors in a system and put them into classes. So that it could be sure that the decision made by the neural network was the best one, a thorough analysis was done with a lot of different ways to set up the number of hidden layers. To design a smart model Electrical Fault Detection for Industry 4.0 using Fusion deep Learning Algorithm Simulations have shown that a neural network can reliably find and classify problems in transmission lines.

articleTitle: Safety Solution Implementation for an Omnidirectional Autonomous Mobile Robot used in Logistics Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper aims to describe the development of a safety solution for an omnidirectional autonomous mobile robot actuated by permanent magnet synchronous machines drives that performs numerous tasks in logistics environments. This is done with specific equipment that ensures a level of safety integrity of type SIL2 or SIL3 according to the IEC 61508 standard, which certifies certain parameters such as probability of dangerous failure on request, risk reduction factor and hourly probability of hazardous malfunctions. The safety system implemented in autonomous mobile robot is a mix between hardware components(locomotion system, perception system, and decision controllers) and software components that use the information from the perception system to generate commands for the locomotion system.

articleTitle: Voltage Control Strategy Using the Rule-Based Reasoning in LV Distribution Networks with PV Penetration Integrating OLTC-Fitted Transformer
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: A voltage control strategy using the rule-based reasoning (RBR) for On-load Tap Changer (OLTC)-fitted transformer, which could be integrated successfully into the low voltage electric distribution networks (LV EDNs) with different photovoltaic (PV) penetration degrees, has been proposed in the paper. Testing their efficiency has been done in a real LV EDN belonging to a Romanian Distribution Network Operator. The results of the simulation process indicated an improvement of the voltage quality indicators (the maximum voltage and the average voltage deviation during the analyzed period, 24 hours, at the end-users level) following the application of the RBR, mitigating the intermittency of injected powers by the PV prosumers with the positive impact on the operation of the LV EDNs. Also, the limit threshold of the penetration degree (50%) identified over which the efficiency of the proposed voltage control strategy integrating OLTC-fitted transformer decreases, considering the input data and the working assumptions used in the simulation process.

articleTitle: Memory Training Interface for Elderly based on Mobile APP
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Currently, the world population is aging rapidly and one of the characteristics that will accompany this new generation of elderly people is the concept of “aging in place”, which means aging at home. The quality of life of the elderly in their home depends on the maintenance of their cognitive and motor skills and, therefore, the way to encourage them to remain autonomous and reduce institutionalization is by training their memory. To help on solving problems like cognitive decline in elderly population it was developed a memory training mobile application based on life story work. The APP has the contribution of many professionals and was validated with a small group of elderly users. Analysis of the collected data is presented in the work to underline the effectiveness of developed APP on cognitive training.

articleTitle: Design and modeling considerations for developing a millimolar Oxalic Acid detection sensor based on screen-printed carbon electrode and methilbenzenpirol
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference and Exposition on Electrical And Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Oxalic acid (OA) has been recognized as a key indicator for the diagnosis of kidney stones. Non-enzymatic electrochemical sensors are required for OA, especially those manufactured on various screen-printed electrodes modified with nanomaterials that ensure simplicity and speed in manufacturing and accuracy in use. Here we propose a sensor design based on a screen-printed carbon electrode (SPCE) made of carbon nanofiber paste (CNF) and conductive polymer methylbenzenpyrrole, that has been meticulously studied by modeling and experimental analysis to obtain the most feasible solution for an OA detection sensor with millimolar precision. The developed sensor reached a limit of detection (LoD) of 0.5 mM of oxalic acid with a quasi-linear characteristic.
